notes: Question IDs are never sent to the model; answers return under the same IDs.
Stage A runs on every comment. Stage B runs only on comments where stage A clears the gate threshold.
Criteria option names are stable enum values. Rewording any instruction or criterion text bumps schema_version and invalidates thresholds.
No question asks Jev to compute or compare dates. Timestamps, horizons-to-years, and resolution windows are computed in code.

stage_a_packed_template._comment: One request per packed state of N comments. Code renders this template once per comment ID (c01..cNN). Keep instructions short: this text is billed once per comment.

is_prediction_{id}.instructions: Does comment {id} make a prediction about what will happen in the future?

criteria.true: Comment {id} claims something will or will not happen later: a technology, company, product, market, law, or social trend
criteria.false: Comment {id} only describes the present or past, gives an opinion or advice, asks a question, or jokes without a real forecast

is_prediction.instructions: Does the comment make a prediction about what will happen in the future?

criteria.true: The comment claims something will or will not happen later: a technology, company, product, market, law, or social trend
criteria.false: The comment only describes the present or past, gives an opinion or advice, asks a question, or jokes without a real forecast

is_checkable.instructions: Could a reasonable person decide years later whether this prediction came true?

criteria.true: The prediction names a concrete outcome that later events could confirm or refute
criteria.false: The prediction is too vague, unfalsifiable, or purely a matter of taste to check

is_sarcastic.instructions: Is the prediction meant sarcastically or as a joke rather than sincerely?

is_conditional.instructions: Does the prediction depend on an explicit condition, such as 'if X happens, then Y'?

direction.instructions: What kind of outcome does the comment predict for its subject?

criteria.success: The subject will grow, win, be adopted, or succeed
criteria.failure: The subject will shrink, lose, be abandoned, or fail
criteria.change: Something will change or happen, without a clear success or failure framing
criteria.no_change: Things will stay the same; a hyped change will not happen

domain.instructions: Which area is the prediction mainly about?

criteria.language_or_framework: Programming languages, frameworks, libraries, developer tools
criteria.company_fate: A specific company's survival, growth, acquisition, or decline
criteria.product_adoption: Whether a product, platform, or device will be adopted
criteria.ai_ml: Artificial intelligence, machine learning, automation of work
criteria.crypto_finance: Cryptocurrency, markets, prices, startup funding, the economy
criteria.policy_law: Regulation, courts, government, privacy law, antitrust
criteria.infrastructure: Cloud, hardware, chips, networks, energy, operating systems
criteria.society_work: Jobs, careers, education, remote work, culture, media

horizon.instructions: Over what time frame does the comment expect the prediction to play out?

criteria.under_1y: Within about a year, or 'soon' / 'next release'
criteria.over_10y: More than ten years, 'eventually', or 'in our lifetime'
criteria.unstated: No time frame stated or implied

stance_vs_thread.instructions: Compared with the parent comment and story title shown in the state, is this prediction going with or against the prevailing view?

criteria.agrees: Supports or extends the view in the parent comment or story
criteria.contrarian: Pushes back on the view in the parent comment or story
criteria.unclear: No clear relationship to a prevailing view

certainty.instructions: How certain does the commenter sound about the prediction?
criteria: Emphatic: 'guaranteed', 'mark my words', 'there is no way'

specificity.instructions: How specific is the predicted outcome?
criteria: Vague direction only: 'this will be big'
Named subject with a general outcome
Named subject, concrete outcome, rough time frame
Named subject, measurable outcome, explicit time frame or number

stage_b_subject_choice._comment: Optional. Jev cannot extract free-text entities, so the subject is a Choice over a curated roster (max 255 options). Build the roster from the pilot's hand labels plus a frequency pass over story titles. 'other' is mandatory; its rate is a pilot metric.

subject.instructions: Which company, product, or technology is the main subject of the prediction?

criteria.google: Google or Alphabet and its products
criteria.deep_learning: Deep learning, neural networks, AI models
